subject: Placeholder environment block textures for the cyberpunk / megacity levels: panels, vents, grating, pipes, fan, hazard stripes, walkway top, girders, crates, barrel, lit sign, windows and screen, lamps, control box.
visual_approach: Programmer pixel art: hard edges, no antialiasing, mid-tone grey panels with dark seams and 1 px highlight / shade bevels, following the owner's dev atlas; colours from the project's shared palette.

generation_settings.palette: 41 hex constants in the script, all from the project's shared palette (not in the repository)

creative_seed.note: No generator seed. The script uses random.Random with fixed per-tile seeds (4, 12, 15, 17 and per-call seeds in its helpers) for small details such as rain streaks and rust spots, so every rebuild is identical.

style_inheritance: First version. Look follows the owner's dev atlas (atlas-dev.png, not in the repository): grey panels, dark seams, amber hazard stripes.
post_analysis_notes: The analysis prompt separated rows with ' / '; the analyst read these as alternate names. There are 28 distinct tiles, named in blocks-placeholder.json.
pipe-elbow alignment: a script check found 0 mismatched pixels where its right edge meets pipe-h and its bottom edge meets pipe-v.

post_analysis.provenance: Post-generation subagent visual analysis; not part of the original generation prompt.
post_analysis.subject: A 7 columns x 4 rows texture atlas of 28 pixel-art tiles (64x64 each) for industrial/cyberpunk environment blocks: metal panels, tile wall, vents, grilles, pipes, fan, hazard stripes, walkway, truss, braced panels, a green control cabinet, barrel, lit signs/windows/screen, wall light, warning lamp, and a control box.
post_analysis.composition: Regular grid with no gaps. Each tile is a self-contained front-on (orthographic, flat) view. Several tiles are split into 2x2 or 2x3 sub-cells (panel-quad, lit-window, walkway-top). Pipes and truss run edge to edge so they can join across tile borders. Three tiles (barrel, lit-sign, wall-light) have a small dark or shadow margin around the main object.
post_analysis.environment: No scene. Tiles are flat surfaces: grey steel panel backgrounds for most, with dark charcoal recessed backgrounds behind pipes, truss and braces. This reads as a sci-fi industrial interior.
post_analysis.colors: Dominant desaturated olive-grey and dark charcoal. Accents are amber/orange and yellow (vent slats, hazard stripes, windows, sign, fan-heater glow), teal-green with rust spots (teal pipe), magenta/pink (screen), red (barrel bands, warning lamp), cyan and red buttons (control box), olive green (cabinet), and a brown/tan checker (tile wall).
post_analysis.materials: Painted or brushed grey metal with faint vertical scratch marks. Riveted steel plates. Glossy cylindrical chrome/steel pipes with highlights. Weathered teal pipe with orange rust flecks and brass-coloured clamps. Perforated mesh and grating. Glowing emissive amber and magenta surfaces. Glassy red lamp dome inside a cage. Matt olive-green painted cabinet. Ceramic or brick-like brown tiles.
post_analysis.lighting: Simple, consistent top-left highlight and bottom-right shadow bevels on frames and pipes. Emissive tiles (vent-louvre slats, grille-panel glow, sign, windows, screen, wall-light, lamp) have flat glow with dithered halo or shadow patches. No cast scene lighting. Overall flat and tile-friendly.
standout_features: Metal elbow pipe curving from the bottom edge up and out to the right edge, with a clamp
Teal rusty pipe with two brass clamps
Amber and black hazard stripe tile and half-height hazard edge
Round industrial fan with 4-5 blades in a square frame
Red warning lamp in a cage with dithered red halo
Pink/magenta glowing screen with scan lines and a square
Yellow sign with blocky garbled glyphs
Steel barrel with two red bands
Control box with small screen, red and cyan buttons, keypad and lever
Diagonal truss with riveted top and bottom chords
important_details: Row 1 tile 1 (panel-plain): plain grey panel with faint scratches - recognisable.
Row 1 tile 2 (panel-riveted): grey panel with rivets around the border - recognisable.
Row 1 tile 3 (panel-quad): four sub-panels with a cross seam and small centre dots - recognisable.
Row 1 tile 4 (tile-wall): brown/tan checker of small square tiles with some rust drips - recognisable, though its colour is warmer than the rest of the atlas.
Row 1 tile 5 (vent-louvre): framed rectangular vent with horizontal amber and grey slats - recognisable as a vent. The amber glow is strong, so it also reads as a heater.
Row 1 tile 6 (vent-grille): horizontal dark slotted band between two plain panels - recognisable.
Row 1 tile 7 (grille-panel): framed diagonal mesh with an orange glowing lower half - recognisable as a mesh or heater grille, not a plain grille panel.
Row 2 tile 1 (grating): dark square-hole grid, full tile - recognisable.
Row 2 tile 2 (pipe-h): horizontal steel pipe with one clamp on a dark background - recognisable.
Row 2 tile 3 (pipe-v): vertical steel pipe with a clamp near the top - recognisable.
Row 2 tile 4 (pipe-elbow): quarter-bend from the bottom to the right, with a clamp - recognisable. The pipe's bottom end is at the tile's bottom edge near the centre-left, not at the exact centre.
Row 2 tile 5 (pipe-teal-h): horizontal teal pipe with rust spots and brass clamps - recognisable.
Row 2 tile 6 (pipe-rail): two vertical posts and horizontal rails with an amber dash strip at the bottom - recognisable as a railing, not a pipe.
Row 2 tile 7 (fan): round fan in a square frame - recognisable.
Row 3 tile 1 (hazard-stripe): full diagonal amber/black stripes - recognisable.
Row 3 tile 2 (hazard-edge): stripe band along the top over a plain panel - recognisable.
Row 3 tile 3 (walkway-top): grey surface with a pale cyan-blue water-like strip on top, over a riveted edge, then plain panel - ambiguous. The blue strip suggests water or ice, not a walkway.
Row 3 tile 4 (truss): diagonal zigzag bracing between riveted chords - recognisable.
Row 3 tile 5 (cross-brace): dark framed panel with an X brace and a centre bolt - recognisable.
Row 3 tile 6 (crate): grey panel with orange corner hazards, an X brace and a centre bolt - reads as a braced crate, though it looks much like cross-brace.
Row 3 tile 7 (crate-green): olive-green cabinet with a faded 'FLI' label and two toggle switches - reads as a locker or cabinet. The label and switches are not typical of a crate.
Row 4 tile 1 (barrel): steel barrel with red bands - recognisable.
Row 4 tile 2 (lit-sign): glowing yellow sign with garbled glyphs - recognisable as a sign, but the text is not legible.
Row 4 tile 3 (lit-window): six amber windows in a 2x3 layout, one dimmed - recognisable.
Row 4 tile 4 (lit-screen): magenta screen with scan lines - recognisable.
Row 4 tile 5 (wall-light): amber light strip in a housing with a dithered light cone below - recognisable.
Row 4 tile 6 (warning-lamp): red caged lamp with a halo - recognisable.
Row 4 tile 7 (control-box): console with a screen, buttons, keypad and lever - recognisable.
post_analysis.synopsis: A coherent, readable placeholder atlas of 28 industrial cyberpunk tiles in a consistent pixel-art style with a muted grey base and bright accent colours. Most tiles are clearly identifiable. A few have identity problems: walkway-top, crate, crate-green, grille-panel and vent-louvre are ambiguous or look different from their names. There are 28 tiles in the image, while the intended list has 25 entries plus slash-alternates.

findings.issue: Tile content does not match the intended name: the blue water-like strip on top does not read as a walkway surface
findings.impact: May be mistaken for water or ice, and may not tile or walk as a platform

findings.issue: Tile looks almost the same as cross-brace, with added hazard corners, so the two are hard to tell apart
findings.impact: Little visual difference between two intended tiles

findings.issue: Green cabinet with a label and switches reads as a locker or electrical cabinet, not a crate
Framed mesh with an orange glow reads as a heater or furnace grille, not a plain grille panel
Garbled blocky glyphs in the sign are not legible text
findings.impact: Fine for a placeholder, but will read as nonsense text

findings.issue: Faint 'FLI' label has odd letter shapes
The elbow pipe is a little off-centre and may not line up with neighbouring pipe-v or pipe-h tiles at the edges
Tile uses warm brown, which does not match the cool grey palette of the other tiles

defect_analysis.overall: No major structural, floating-object, distortion, perspective or lighting defects. Highlights and shadows are consistent across tiles. The only issues are name-to-content mismatches on a few tiles and minor legibility or tiling concerns.

mismatches_or_uncertainties: The atlas shows 28 tiles. The intended list has 25 names, plus several slash-alternates (grille-panel / grating, fan / hazard-stripe, crate-green / barrel), so the exact row-major mapping is uncertain.
My mapping of names to tiles is my best guess, and the order could differ if the alternates are meant as separate tiles.
Whether the blue strip in walkway-top is intended to be a lit edge or something else is uncertain.
I could not verify seamless tiling of tile edges from this single view.
